data.why: CORN ships a built-in demo project (examples/demo/documents.csv + project.yaml) installable from the home screen's 'Install demo project' button, so no external or synthetic data is needed.

goals: install the built-in demo project and build its runtime cache so documents can be queried
review documents in the corpus and filter them using project-defined metadata fields
mark exact-span evidence text in a document and attach it to a source-target relationship (tie)
build out a node-to-node relationship network across multiple documents with tie labels and optional attributes
save pending annotations for a workspace/annotator scope and export them as an edge-list CSV or JSON archive
import or export a single document's annotation JSON to check portability of the annotation format

review.summary: The tree follows CORN's core manual workflow faithfully: set up the project, query the corpus, code source→target ties with exact-span or note evidence, save with validation, and export scoped edge lists. The screens I opened support it, and on CSV attributes it is more accurate than the replay. It leaves out the README's project-creation wizard and the human-vs-LLM review and reporting, and it splits query filters too finely, so it needs those additions and merges before filing.
